thread:
taylor: Quick sync in 5 about the PM actions for alert noise & paging patterns. Link: https://redwood.internal/postmortems/pm-2026-03-recurring-pages

taylor: Need to confirm owners, smallest safe changes, and verification plan.

devon: Posting current action set from the doc so we can reassign if needed:
- ACT-101: raise svc-ingest error-rate threshold from 1% -> 1.5% (owner: maria) due 2026-05-04
- ACT-102: consolidate kafka-lag alerts by consumer_group (owner: sam) due 2026-04-30
- ACT-103: quiet-window + suppression for nightly-batch (owner: jordan) due 2026-05-07
- ACT-104: A/B rollout of probabilistic-dedupe (owner: lina) due 2026-05-15

maria: I can take ACT-101 but it's blocked until infra gives a canary slot and a metrics baseline.

sam: For ACT-102, request: change fingerprinting from `topic+partition` -> `consumer_group|lag_bucket`. This maps better to operator impact. Example: 
```
fingerprint: ["consumer_group","lag_bucket"]
dedupe_window: 10m
```

jordan: Ops asked quiet-window 01:30-04:00 UTC for backfills. Any objections?

lina: For the experiment, plan: staging -> 5% prod -> 25% prod, 72h per phase. Monitor pagers/sec and dedupe-hit ratio. Rollback criteria: pager rate +30% or FP increase > 15%.

ops-bot: @maria canary slot reserved: 2026-04-27 23:00-01:00 UTC. Runbook updated: https://playbooks.redwood/runbooks/alert-tuning-v2

devon: Can someone volunteer to own post-deploy verification checks? Need: 1) pager cadence check, 2) sample traces for suppressed alerts, 3) false-positive audit.

maria: I'll do the first-week verification and post findings.

sam: I'll open a PR for the kafka dedupe rule today and tag eng-oncall for review.

jordan: I'll draft the quiet-window config and include an override for emergency jobs.

lina: I'll wire dashboards: dedupe effectiveness, suppressed pager count, and FP trend. Will share links before rollout.

taylor: Great. I'll create tracking tickets (ENGOPS-3425 etc.) and own the timeline. Standing check-in Thursday 15:00 UTC. Post short updates as replies under the PM doc. :white_check_mark:
